ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, a sealed container holds a certain mass of carbon dioxide. When the volume $V$ (in cubic meters, $m^{3}$) of the container changes, the density $\rho$ (in kilograms per cubic meter, $kg/m^{3}$) of the gas changes accordingly. It is known that the relationship between density $\rho$ and volume $V$ is an inverse proportion, as depicted in the graph. When $V = 5m^{3}$, $\rho = 1.98kg/m^{3}$. For $3 \leq V \leq 9$, determine the range of the carbon dioxide density $\rho$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} By observing the function graph, it is known that $\rho$ decreases with the increase of $V$,\\
when $V=3\,m^{3}$, $\rho=\frac{9.9}{3}=3.3\,kg/m^{3}$,\\
when $V=9\,m^{3}$, $\rho=\frac{9.9}{9}=1.1\,kg/m^{3}$,\\
$\therefore$ when $3\le V\le 9$, $1.1\le \rho \le 3.3\,(kg/m^{3})$\\
That is, the range of change in the density of carbon dioxide $\rho$ is $\boxed{1.1\le \rho \le 3.3\,(kg/m^{3})}$.

When the volume $V$ (in cubic meters, $m^{3}$) of the container changes, the density $\rho$ (in kilograms per cubic meter, $kg/m^{3}$) of the gas changes accordingly. It is known that the relationship between density $\rho$ and volume $V$ is an inverse proportion, as depicted in the graph. When $V = 5m^{3}$, $\rho = 1.98kg/m^{3}$. For $3 \leq V \leq 9$, determine the range of the carbon dioxide density $\rho$.
ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer:
\textbf{Solution:} By observing the function graph, it is known that $\rho$ decreases with the increase of $V$,\\
when $V=3\,m^{3}$, $\rho=\frac{9.9}{3}=3.3\,kg/m^{3}$,\\
when $V=9\,m^{3}$, $\rho=\frac{9.9}{9}=1.1\,kg/m^{3}$,\\
$\therefore$ when $3\le V\le 9$, $1.1\le \rho \le 3.3\,(kg/m^{3})$\\
That is, the range of change in the density of carbon dioxide $\rho$ is $\boxed{1.1\le \rho \le 3.3\,(kg/m^{3})}$

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the vertical axis is labeled ρ/(kg/m^3), and the horizontal axis is labeled V/m^3; the curve is located in the first quadrant and has the shape of an inverse proportional function decreasing to the right, indicating that when the volume V increases, the density ρ decreases. Reasoning: From the meaning of the problem, ρ is inversely proportional to V, let ρ = k/V. It is known that when V = 5 m^3, ρ = 1.98 kg/m^3, so k = 5 × 1.98 = 9.9, therefore ρ = 9.9/V. Since this function decreases as V increases when V > 0, on 3 ≤ V ≤ 9, the maximum value occurs at V = 3, ρ = 9.9/3 = 3.3; the minimum value occurs at V = 9, ρ = 9.9/9 = 1.1. Therefore the density range is 1.1 ≤ ρ ≤ 3.3 kg/m^3.
